Deepen the void so it reads as a usable open-space figure rather than a shallow subtraction.
Align the open side to the access edge indicated by the program context.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the existing public void into a clearer courtyard-like figure while preserving the bent primary mass and the access-aligned ancestry.
Increase the courtyard carve slightly to make the open ground more legible and usable.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent bent-and-bridged mass in all four views, with a single dominant bar that turns and frames a large interior void. The open space is legible and aligned to the verified access edge, so the ground response is programmatically positive rather than sealed. The silhouette is not a literal stair-stack; it is a continuous bent section with a modest upper bridge/cantilever, which fits neighborhood living better than a pure sculptural object. The main weakness is that the section remains fairly generic and box-derived, so it is competent rather than strongly sectional; still, it supports the brief and survives the hard gates.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing with a large carved center and a lifted connector creates a legible public void while preserving a compact datum.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much more circular and site-anchored than the candidate; do not copy the ring geometry.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A low perimeter ring around a central open court reinforces public space and clear edge conditions.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Aerial/site-complex scale is much broader than the candidate's compact massing.

A rectangular body relieved by a large cutout and overhang gives a strong ground threshold and public opening.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated mass with a central courtyard and a folded/active roof can support neighborhood-scale mixed use.
